task: One merchant facade average-neutral warm ivory plaster modulation A/B
scope: Exactly one 02_market_house static imported plaster surface role, two material surfaces; no geometry, door/window hole, collision, light, camera, exposure, other surface or world scene change
root_bitmap_note: 1254px warm ivory source is not proven naturally seamless and would change the authored cream wall hue if multiplied as-is.

candidate_modulation.method: Desaturate to luminance only, use 40 percent of the source brightness deviation, clip factor0.96..1.025 around grayscale sRGB248, then compensate actual Godot glTF material albedo numeric mean

fixture.engine: Godot 4.7.2 Forward+ Vulkan actual NVIDIA RTX 5080 capture
fixture.camera_pair: same 55deg FOV, eye-height1.62m, target and exposure for street14m and upper-close7.5m shots
fixture.process_status: both bounded Godot trees exit0; all_members_exited=true, active_processes=0

preserved_rejected_first_trial.reason: Used linear mean0.939 to compensate imported glTF material whose actual Godot albedo color numerics are sRGB-like. Real plaster ROI street +4.49/+4.99/+4.60 RGB/255 and close +4.42/+4.43/+4.86, making the wall brighter rather than mean-neutral.

current_mean_neutral_trial.compensation: divide imported baseline albedo numerics by actual normalized bitmap mean sRGB248.04/255 instead of linear0.939

visual_assessment: Root inspected the actual v2 street and upper-close same-camera Godot pairs. Color is preserved, but street-view visual benefit is very small. Root decided not to adopt this modulation in the main scene. The source bitmap, normalized derivative and both failed/mean-neutral fixture receipts remain for provenance; no further parameter sweep is planned.
root_visual_decision: Do not adopt in the current game/world; no texture or override added to main modular assets.
